manifest_meta.title: Corvan Grain: October sea shipments down 62% on last year

paragraphs.raw_text: DOC_ID: ORV-0021 EVENT_ID: E5 TITLE: Corvan Grain: October sea shipments down 62% on last year SOURCE_NAME: Corvan Grain SOURCE_TYPE: company_statement RELIABILITY: 2 PUB_DATE: 2026-11-12 PUB_TIME: 10:30 COUNTRY: Orvan SECTOR: Wheat LANGUAGE: en --- Corvan Grain: October sea shipments down 62% on last year
[P1] Corvan Grain reports that its sea shipments of wheat and maize in October 2026 were 62% below the same month a year earlier.
[P2] The fall follows the end of the Corridor Agreement on 10 September and the strike at Orvan Grain Port that began on 14 September.
[P3] The company has moved some cargoes to the Ravik Rail Link and to road haulage. Rail capacity is limited and cannot replace the sea route.
[P4] "We are shipping what we can and telling buyers the truth about the rest," a company spokesperson said.

[P5] The statement is unusual for the firm, which normally leaves monthly figures to the trade press. A spokesperson said the company wanted to correct what it called exaggerated accounts of the disruption. The company has not changed its contracts with Midgard or Tolan buyers, and it says it is honouring them where shipping allows. It has also warned that the rail alternative is expensive and that some cargoes will arrive late. The firm will not give a forecast for the first quarter.

[P6] The company's statement does not give a monthly breakdown by product, and it does not say how much of the fall is due to the strike rather than the end of the agreement. It says both mattered. The figures are for its own shipments, not for the port as a whole.
[P7] Corvan Grain will publish its November figures in the normal cycle.
